items.title: After an admissible blowup of a compactification, a morphism of finite type separated over the base extends to a proper morphism from an open containing the original
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S, a scheme U of finite type and separated over S, a quasi-compact open V of U with a compactification V inside Y over S, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowup Y' -> Y and an open V inside V' inside Y' such that V -> U extends to a proper morphism V' -> U (statement lines 9761-9769). The proof forms the scheme theoretic image Z of the diagonal morphism V -> Y x_S U, and uses two inputs in sequence: that replacing Y by a V-admissible blowup replaces Z by the corresponding strict transform, which is exactly the strict transform comparison lemma proven just before, and then the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, which allows one to assume Z -> Y is an open immersion (proof lines 9772-9777). If V' denotes the image of Z in Y, then V' -> U is proper because the projection Y x_S U -> U is proper and V' is isomorphic to the closed subscheme Z of that fibre product (proof lines 9778-9781). Chaining the strict transform comparison with the Zariski-after-blowup input to make the image an open immersion is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
